KR.read: Korea's dermocosmetics segment now has a size anchor, but the Korean sources disagree sharply. Samjong KPMG (via Korea Herald) puts the market at KRW 4.5tn in 2020 (MEDIUM, RETAIL); the Korean Enterprise Reputation Research body also cites KRW 4.5tn but for 2022, with KRW 5.5tn projected for 2025; and a cosmeceutical institute gives a much lower KRW 1.2tn for 2020. That is a definitional tangle — 'dermocosmetics/cosmeceutical' is drawn differently by each — so the figure is anchored around the low-single-digit KRW-trillions but not pinned. Euromonitor's HIGH-confidence +13% YoY growth (2024) still stands as the most reliable single datapoint.
KR.trend: Euromonitor reports +13% YoY for 2024 (HIGH, RETAIL), driven by actives (PDRN, exosomes, peptides) — the segment is growing fast. The KERI series (KRW 4.5tn 2022 to a projected 5.5tn 2025) implies continued growth, but is MEDIUM and definitionally loose; no clean derma-specific CAGR forecast is available.
KR.caveats: The size figures conflict by up to ~4x depending on how 'dermocosmetics' is scoped, and several are recorded on an NA basis because the source definition was unclear — treat scale as indicative; the growth read (Euromonitor, HIGH) is the firmer signal.

IN.read: India dermocosmetics is anchored by P&S Market Research at US$0.28bn (2024, RETAIL, LOW) — but that is a narrow, Rx-adjacent definition (US$256mn 2023 base, ~10.3% CAGR to US$505mn 2030). A much broader competing estimate (MarkWide US$1.85bn 2026, ~11.6% CAGR) is roughly 7x larger, a pure definitional gap. A masstige-tier-only cut (Expert Market Research US$65.55mn 2025, 14.6% CAGR) sits below both. Derma-D2C revenue is now on file too (Minimalist Rs347cr FY24, NET_REALISATION).
IN.trend: All reads point to fast growth — forecast CAGRs span ~10% (P&S, narrow) to ~15% (EMR, masstige) — but every one is a LOW-confidence forecast, not observed growth. Minimalist's Rs184cr (FY23) to Rs347cr (FY24) revenue jump is a single-company signal, not the segment's rate.
IN.caveats: The ~7x spread between the narrow (P&S) and broad (MarkWide) sizings means India dermocosmetics scale is genuinely unresolved in the data; all sources are LOW confidence with differing organised/Rx scope.

combined.read: Both sides now carry a value_usd_bn size, so a rough comparison is possible — Korea (KRW ~4.5tn ≈ US$3bn, MEDIUM) is an order of magnitude larger than India's narrow US$0.28bn read, and still larger than India's broad US$1.85bn read — but both sides are definitionally unstable (KR sources ~4x apart, IN sources ~7x apart), so this is directional, not a firm ratio. The more decision-relevant fact is momentum plus corridor fit: both markets are growing double-digit, and dermocosmetics is the corridor's highest-conviction whitespace (mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3). Fresh corridor evidence — Nykaa's K-beauty GMV +60% YoY (Q3 2025), Medicube/Illiyoon/Aestura launching on Nykaa/Tira through 2026 — confirms the pull, though no India brand-level K-derma revenue is published yet.
